question: redirects
answer:
HTTPX disables automatic redirect following by default. Set `follow_redirects=True` on the client or per request to enable it. [docs/compatibility.md](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/docs/compatibility.md:8)

- `Client` and `AsyncClient` both use `send()` → `_send_handling_auth()` → `_send_handling_redirects()`. The redirect loop calls `_send_single_request()` for each hop, records prior responses in `response.history`, and raises `TooManyRedirects` if the configured limit is exceeded. With following enabled, it consumes the redirect response via `read()` or `aread()` before sending the next request. Otherwise, it returns the response with `response.next_request` set. [httpx/_client.py (sync)](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:879) · [httpx/_client.py (async)](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:1594)
- `Response.has_redirect_location` requires a `Location` header and status `301`, `302`, `303`, `307`, or `308`. [httpx/_models.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_models.py:772)
- `BaseClient._build_redirect_request()` uses `_redirect_method()` to switch `POST` on `301` and non-`HEAD` methods on `302` or `303` to `GET`. `_redirect_url()` resolves relative locations and carries forward the original fragment when needed. `_redirect_headers()` updates `Host` on origin changes, strips cross-origin `Authorization` except for direct HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrades, and replaces the original `Cookie` header using the client’s cookie jar. When the method switches to `GET`, `_redirect_headers()` removes body framing headers and `_redirect_stream()` drops the body. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/httpx-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:475)
